intro: Small Python authoring API. Use request for HTTP data, context for helpers/in-memory state/persistent state, and input for the previous node output.

groups.title: Functions you write
groups.summary: Fixed function names. Keep the signatures as shown.

entries.name: run(input, request, context, params)
entries.summary: Custom node body. Return the value for the next step.

details.label: When
details.text: Called exactly once per request that reaches this node in the policy graph.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `input` — output of the previous node, or `None` at the start
- `request` — the current HTTP request (read/redirect/block)
- `context` — shared state + logging + notifications
- `params` — dict of values configured on this node in the UI

details.label: Returns
details.text: Any value you want. The next node or operator receives it as its `input`.

details.label: Side effects
details.text:
- Call `request.block(...)` to stop the request with an HTTP response
- Call `request.redirect(...)` to change the outbound URL
- Write to `context.state` to share data with later nodes
- Call `context.log(...)` to emit an event to Observability
- Call `context.notify(...)` to send a UI notification

entries.name: triggered_by(request)
entries.summary: Start node gate. Return True to run the policy, False to skip.

details.label: When
details.text: Evaluated before the policy runs. If it returns `False`, the entire policy is skipped for this request.

details.label: Args
details.text: - `request` — the current HTTP request (read-only here; don't block or redirect)

details.label: Returns
details.text: `True` to enter the policy (routes to `next`), `False` to skip it.

details.label: Side effects
details.text: None. Keep this a pure check — no mutations, no logging.

entries.name: if_condition(input)
entries.summary: If operator. True → then branch, False → else branch.

details.label: When
details.text: Called when the policy reaches an If operator. It only picks a branch — it cannot change `input`.

details.label: Args
details.text: - `input` — output of the previous node

details.label: Returns
details.text: `True` routes to the `then` port, `False` routes to the `else` port.

details.label: Side effects
details.text: None. Operators only route; the same `input` is forwarded unchanged.

entries.name: switch_condition(input)
entries.summary: Switch operator. Return a case label to choose the output port.

details.label: When
details.text: Called when the policy reaches a Switch operator. It picks which output port to follow.

details.label: Args
details.text: - `input` — output of the previous node

details.label: Returns
details.text: A string matching one of the configured case labels. If no match, the `default` port is used (when present).

details.label: Side effects
details.text: None. Operators only route; the same `input` is forwarded unchanged.

groups.title: request
groups.summary: Current HTTP request. Read it, redirect it, or block it.

entries.name: request.method
entries.summary: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.).

entries.name: request.host
entries.summary: Host name, e.g. www.youtube.com.

details.label: Example
details.text: `request.host.endswith(".reddit.com")`

entries.name: request.url
entries.summary: Full URL. Assign to redirect.

details.label: Read
details.text: Returns the complete URL including scheme, host, path, and query.

details.label: Write
details.text: Setting `request.url = "..."` redirects the outbound request to that URL.

entries.name: request.path
entries.summary: Path + query string, e.g. /shorts/abc?v=1.

details.label: Example
details.text: `"/shorts" in request.path`

entries.name: request.headers
entries.summary: HTTP headers. Use .get(name, default).

details.label: Example
details.text: `request.headers.get("referer", "")`

entries.name: request.text()
entries.summary: Request body decoded as UTF-8 text.

details.label: Returns
details.text: The decoded body string. Returns `""` if the body is empty or unreadable.

entries.name: request.redirect(url)
entries.summary: Change the outbound request target.

details.label: Args
details.text: - `url` — the new destination URL (string)

details.label: Effect
details.text: The proxy sends the request to this URL instead of the original.

entries.name: request.block(status, message)
entries.summary: Stop the request and return a plain-text response to the client.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `status` — HTTP status code (e.g. `403`)
- `message` — plain-text body sent back to the client

details.label: Effect
details.text: The request never reaches the internet. The policy stops after the current node.

groups.title: context
groups.summary: Shared helpers: in-memory state, persistent state, logging, and notifications.

entries.name: context.state[key]
entries.summary: Shared in-memory key/value store for this proxy session.

details.label: What
details.text: A dict-like store that persists across nodes and requests within the same proxy session only. It is cleared when the proxy process restarts.

details.label: Usage
details.text:
- `context.state["counter"] = 0` — write a value
- `val = context.state["counter"]` — read a value (raises `KeyError` if missing)
- Values are kept by reference: mutating a stored list/dict is visible to all later nodes

entries.name: context.state.get(key, default)
entries.summary: Read state safely, returning default when key is missing.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `key` — string key
- `default` — value returned when key is absent

details.label: Example
details.text: `count = context.state.get("visits", 0)`

entries.name: context.state.setdefault(key, value)
entries.summary: Get existing value or insert a default and return it.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `key` — string key
- `value` — initial value to store if key is missing

details.label: Example
details.text:
`hits = context.state.setdefault("hits", [])`
`hits.append(request.url)`

entries.name: context.persistent_state.get(keyword)
entries.summary: Read a JSON-backed top-level value. Raises KeyError when missing.

details.label: What
details.text: A raw global store persisted in the app's state JSON file. Values survive proxy restarts.

details.label: Args
details.text: - `keyword` — top-level string key

details.label: Returns
details.text: The value stored under `keyword`. Raises `KeyError` if the key is absent.

details.label: Important
details.text: Mutating a returned nested dict/list has no durable side effect until you call `context.persistent_state.set(keyword, data)` with the updated value.

entries.name: context.persistent_state.set(keyword, data)
entries.summary: Persist a JSON-serializable top-level value.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `keyword` — top-level string key
- `data` — JSON-serializable value to store

details.label: Effect
details.text: Writes the updated state JSON file immediately.

details.label: Raises
details.text: Raises when `data` is not JSON-serializable.

details.label: Example
details.text:
`usage = context.persistent_state.get("usage")`
`usage["reddit"] = {"daily_seconds": {}}`
`context.persistent_state.set("usage", usage)`

entries.name: context.log(type, message, level, **data)
entries.summary: Emit a structured event visible in Observability.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `type` — event type string (shows in the Type column)
- `message` — human-readable description
- `level` — `"info"` (default), `"debug"`, `"warning"`, or `"error"`
- `**data` — any extra keyword args become structured metadata

details.label: Example
details.text: `context.log("match", "Reddit detected", platform="reddit")`

entries.name: context.notify(type, message, level, **data)
entries.summary: Send a native UI notification and log it.

details.label: Args
details.text:
- `type` — notification title / category
- `message` — notification body text
- `level` — `"info"` (default), `"debug"`, `"warning"`, or `"error"`
- `**data` — any extra keyword args become structured metadata

details.label: Effect
details.text: The dashboard shows a native OS notification (when permissions are granted) and the event appears in Observability.

groups.title: params
groups.summary: Configured values for the current node (set in the UI).

entries.name: params[key]
entries.summary: Read a configured parameter by name.

details.label: Args
details.text: - `key` — parameter name as shown in the node's config form

details.label: Returns
details.text: The configured value. Could be a string, number, list, or dict depending on the node.

details.label: Raises
details.text: `KeyError` if the parameter was not configured.

details.label: Tip
details.text: Cast values yourself when needed: `int(params["seconds"])`
